claude.sample_unit: physicians (48-54 discharge summaries and referrals per group)

links.outcome: Document quality and creation time: clinician review/editing of LLM drafts vs clinician-only vs unedited LLM drafts
links.effect: Clinician-in-the-loop outperformed clinician-only in most quality domains; LLM-only drafts fastest but lowest quality. Summaries faster (β = −59.4 s, P = .047); referrals slower (β = 94.8 s, P<.001).
links.quote: LLM-only drafts were fastest but had the lowest quality.

links.effect: 17 physicians; in most quality domains for both document types, clinician-in-the-loop outperformed clinician-only; LLM-only drafts were fastest but had the lowest quality.
links.quote: In most quality domains for both document types, the clinician-in-the-loop workflow outperformed clinician-only drafting.

links.effect: Summaries were shorter with clinician-in-loop (β = −59.4 seconds; 95% CI, −118.1 to −0.8; P = .047), but referrals took longer (β = 94.8 seconds; 95% CI, 40.4 to 149.3; P<.001).
links.quote: For referrals, clinician-in-the-loop required more time (β = 94.8 seconds; 95% CI, 40.4 to 149.3; P<.001).

links.outcome: document quality of unedited versus clinician-reviewed AI drafts
links.effect: LLM-only drafts were fastest but had lowest quality, whereas clinician-in-the-loop review and editing outperformed clinician-only drafting in most quality domains for both summaries and referrals.
links.quote: LLM-only drafts were fastest but had the lowest quality.

screen.practice: clinician review and editing of LLM drafts
screen.reason: This randomized controlled trial explicitly investigates a clinician-in-the-loop workflow (clinician review and editing of LLM-generated drafts) compared to clinician-only drafting and unedited LLM drafts for simulated patient documentation.
